comments.body:
**Assessed and fixed in #752** (merge 8277233f85, head 9c1583ffd7).

**Assessment: the boundary holds.** The Aggressive sandbox on macOS never reaches the keychain service. Seatbelt allows `com.apple.SecurityServer` only in `seatbelt_network_policy.sbpl`, which is added only when network is on or a network proxy runs. Aggressive has network off, and `~/Library/Keychains` is a denied read.

I checked this with real `sandbox-exec` and a disposable keychain file. It was created with `HOME` and `CFFIXED_USER_HOME` pointing at a temp folder; the login keychain and search list were never touched (I compared them before and after). Running `security find-generic-password -s probe736 -w <temp keychain>`:
- outside any sandbox: returns the canary;
- workspace-write sandbox, network on: returns the canary;
- Aggressive's sandbox (network off): `The specified item could not be found` (exit 44), even though the keychain file itself was readable.

So AGG-10's command ran but couldn't read anything. Its output was the same as here. What was wrong was the wording.

**Fix (no sandbox change):** under Aggressive on macOS, with network off and no proxy:
- the prompt for a `security` keychain verb now says the keychain is out of reach of agent commands, and that this is never granted. No Grant once is offered (before, it was offered when no untrusted content had arrived);
- where the command fails, the result says the "could not be found" comes from Aggressive, not from what the keychain holds;
- the inspector lists "using the macOS keychain".

**Regression test:** `core/tests/suite/issue_736_740.rs::issue_736_keychain_is_out_of_reach_and_explained` uses real Seatbelt and a disposable keychain. It fails before the fix and passes after.

**Evidence:** tmux replay `qa/security-levels/fixes/issue-736-740-20261014/`, [video](https://github.com/CorbanuCore/CorbanuTerminal/releases/download/demos/issue-736-issue736-keychain-explained-a79ff79b392a-2026-10-13.mp4).

**Residual, unchanged:** this would need security sign-off to change. If an enterprise requirements file enforces a managed network proxy, Seatbelt adds the network rules, which open the keychain service. Corbanu then makes no keychain claim.

title: Aggressive (AGG-10): `security find-generic-password` runs after approval; the keychain service answers from the sandbox
